'''Axel Claus Heitmann''' (born October 2, 1959) is a German business executive in the [[chemical industry]].

==Life and career==

Born in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]], Heitmann studied [[chemistry]] as an undergraduate at the [[University of Hamburg]]. He went on to earn his doctorate in chemistry from the [[University of Southampton]] in England.<ref name="BW">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130118204659/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=12037746&symbol=LXS:GR|title=BusinessWeek executive profile}}, accessed 12/10/09.</ref>

After being enrolled in a training program at [[Bayer AG]], he held a series of research and development and management jobs in the company’s [[synthetic rubber|rubber]] manufacturing and [[cellulose]] products divisions. In 2002, he rose to the post of head of Bayer’s Rubber Business Group and joined the executive committee of Bayer MaterialScience.<ref name="Dawson">Brad Dawson, “Lanxess’ Top Exec Discusses Firm’s Plans, Progress,” ''Rubber & Plastics News'', October 2, 2006.</ref>

In 2004, when Bayer spun off its rubber and [[specialty chemicals]] businesses into a new company, [[Lanxess AG]], Heitmann was named as chairman of the Board of Management.<ref name="CE">''ChemEurope.com'', “Bayer NewCo to be Named ‘Lanxess,’” March 19, 2004.</ref>

In 2008, he received a Stevie Award for Best Executive in Europe.<ref name="Stevies">[http://www.stevieawards.com The Stevies]: The International Business Awards, accessed 12/10/09.</ref>

Heitmann is married and has two children.<ref name="LXsite">Lanxess website, [http://lanxess.com/en/corporate/about-lanxess/management/board-of-management/dr-axel-claus-heitmann/ “Dr. Axel Claus Heitmann: Curriculum Vitae,”] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608101039/http://lanxess.com/en/corporate/about-lanxess/management/board-of-management/dr-axel-claus-heitmann/ |date=June 8, 2013 }} accessed 12/10/09.</ref>
